pages.title: Codex data is used
pages.text: $(thing)habitat$(), $(thing)activity$(), $(thing)alertness$() and $(thing)feeding_speed$() are not cosmetic:$(br2)$(li)Wrong habitat (fresh vs ocean) removes the fish from the pool.$(br)$(li)Wrong activity window (day / night / rain) reduces its weight.$(br)$(li)Alertness feeds the bite chance; feeding speed sets the reaction window.

pages.title: Two formulas
pages.text: $(bold)Bite chance$() = max(0.05, 0.9 × (1 − alertness × tackle conspicuousness))$(br2)$(bold)Reaction window (s)$() = tolerance ÷ feeding speed × (1 + current resistance × bonus)$(br2)So: the warier the fish and the more conspicuous the tackle, the harder the bite; the faster it feeds, the shorter your window; more anti-current lets you hold longer.

pages.title: Weight roll
pages.text: Weight is sampled from a normal distribution: $(thing)mean$() as the average, $(thing)sigma$() as the deviation (default mean × 0.25), then clamped to $(thing)min$()~$(thing)max$().$(br2)Every catch differs; the steelyard and display stand read the same value.

pages.title: Syncing
pages.text: Codex, tackle and weight data load on the server only. They are pushed to clients on login and on $(thing)/reload$(), and clients rebuild them with $(bold)the same parsing code$().$(br2)What you see in the UI is exactly what the maths uses. If a change does not show up, check that the server actually reloaded.
